# Reference Data

## Definition

Reference Data are sets of permissible values — codes and their meanings — used to classify or categorise other data. They are often defined by external bodies (e.g. country and currency codes) and shared across systems.

## Explanation

Reference data typically realizes a [[Controlled Vocabulary]] or [[Taxonomy]] at the data level. Architectural concerns: authoritative source per code list, versioning and validity periods of codes, mappings between code lists, and distribution ([[Reference Data Hub]]).

Codes change over time: a code can be retired while historical data still uses it. Code lists therefore need their own [[Temporal Data Management|temporal management]].

## Distinctions

- vs [[Master Data]]: see there.
- vs [[Metadata]]: reference data values appear *in* business data.

## Examples

- Country codes, currency codes, claim status codes, product categories.
